title: 9/11’s Long Shadow
gist: A Project Syndicate Big Picture collection arguing that America's response to the September 11, 2001 attacks — not the attacks themselves — is what changed the world, leading the US to abandon the post-Cold War principles that were supposed to shape a better future.

insights.claim: It was America's response to the September 11, 2001 attacks, rather than the attacks themselves, that truly changed the world.
insights.speaker: PS EDITORS
insights.so_what: Frames policy reaction as the dominant variable after a geopolitical shock — the analytical starting point for assessing any future attack's market and policy consequences.
insights.quote: As tragic as the terrorist attacks of September 11, 2001, were, it was America’s response that truly changed the world.
insights.locator: As tragic as the terrorist attacks of September 11

insights.claim: The 9/11 attacks led the United States to abandon the principles that, with the Cold War over, were supposed to shape a better future.
insights.speaker: PS EDITORS
insights.so_what: Locates the origin of today's eroded rules-based order in 2001 rather than in more recent events — relevant to how durable the erosion is.
insights.quote: it seems clear that the event led the United States to abandon the principles that, with the Cold War over, were supposed to shape a better future
insights.locator: As tragic as the terrorist attacks

insights.claim: Attribution is inherently difficult: it is hard to pinpoint precisely which developments over the last 25 years were caused or compounded by 9/11, so the causal claim is directional rather than precise.
insights.speaker: PS EDITORS
insights.so_what: A caution against over-fitting single-event explanations to 25 years of geopolitical change.
insights.quote: it is difficult to pinpoint precisely which developments over the last 25 years were caused or compounded by 9/11
insights.locator: While it is difficult to pinpoint precisely

insights.claim: The collection assembles Timothy Snyder, Anne-Marie Slaughter, Javier Solana, Angel Saz-Carranza and Richard Haass, indicating a cross-Atlantic foreign-policy establishment consensus on the self-inflicted costs of the post-9/11 era.
insights.speaker: PS EDITORS
insights.so_what: When establishment voices converge on a revisionist reading of post-9/11 policy, it lowers the political cost of retrenchment from open-ended security commitments.
